confirmed.title: SX1276 IRQ register is read over bit-banged SPI every loop pass

confirmed.title: Out-of-range WiFi: hard reconnect cycle every 20 s plus perpetual driver auto-reconnect between attempts
confirmed.claim: When disconnected, the loop calls wifiState.connectToPreferred() every WIFI_RETRY_PERIOD_MS=20 s (config.h:72) forever, and the code's own comment says connectToWiFi() hard-cycles the radio (disconnect(true)+begin, WiPhone.ino:1976-1979). Worse, Networks.cpp:519-523 documents that between our retries the Arduino driver auto-reconnects perpetually on 'AP not found', keeping the radio mid-association until the autoswitch scanner's WiFi.disconnect() interrupts it. So a phone carried out of range all day (the September hunt) keeps the WiFi radio actively probing/associating most of the time - likely the single largest field battery drain, dwarfing everything in the loop. The codebase already has the exact backoff pattern needed: _discScans in autoSwitchTick eases scans from 2 min to 5 min after ~10 min of failures and resets on connect/screen-wake (Networks.cpp:494-514). Mirroring that for the reconnect retry (ease 20 s to 2-5 min after sustained absence, immediate retry on screen wake, and a WiFi.disconnect() to quiesce the driver between backed-off attempts) costs nothing in reachability - with no AP in range the phone is SIP-unreachable regardless and LoRa is unaffected. confirmed.title: SIP send path: vsprintf into 500-byte stack buffer, remote-influenced content
confirmed.claim: Connection::print() and Connection::printf() (tinySIP.h:243-267) format with vsprintf into a fixed char buffer[500] on the UI-task stack with no length limit. Call sites pass values parsed from inbound SIP traffic: TCP_PRINTF at tinySIP.cpp:3568 prints respRouteSet[i] (built from the peer's Record-Route headers), and 3583/3606/3611/3621/3625 print display-name + addr-spec + tag from the parsed To/From headers. The RX buffer admits messages up to MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2000 (tinySIP.h:538), so a single inbound INVITE/MESSAGE with a ~600+ char From display name or Record-Route value — which the stack must echo back in its response — overflows the stack frame. The listener is plain WiFiUDP on the LAN, so this is reachable by any LAN peer, not just the proxy. Fix is mechanical: vsnprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer), ...) in both methods; normal VoIP.ms traffic never approaches 500 bytes so behavior in the field is unchanged.

confirmed.title: SIP header parser writes past respHeaderName[100] with no cap check
confirmed.claim: parseAllHeaders() does respHeaderName[respHeaderCnt++] = s (tinySIP.cpp:2389) and respHeaderValue[respHeaderCnt-1] = s (line 2414) with no comparison against MAX_HEADER_CNT=100 (tinySIP.h:540); both arrays are fixed char*[100] members (tinySIP.h:847-848). A minimal header line costs ~5 bytes ('a:b\r\n'), so a 2000-byte message can carry ~380 headers and overwrite pointers well past both arrays into the adjacent TinySIP members (remoteToFromDyn, respTo*, respFrom* at tinySIP.h:849+), i.e. memory corruption from any UDP packet on the LAN. Fix: bail out (or stop storing) when respHeaderCnt reaches MAX_HEADER_CNT — a 3-line guard that can never trigger on legitimate traffic (real SIP messages carry ~10-20 headers).

The parse loop walks buff, sized MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2000 (tinySIP.h:538,828). A minimal well-formed header 'a:b\r\n' is 5 bytes and increments respHeaderCnt each time (malformed headers hit the skipCharLiteral colon check and abort, but well-formed ones do not), so a 2000-byte message produces ~380 stored entries, writing ~280 pointers past respHeaderName[100] into respHeaderValue[] and the adjacent member pointers — real memory corruption. Value high (LAN-triggerable corruption), risk low (guard is inert on legitimate traffic), effort small.

confirmed.title: Early heap-step hypothesis A: notification pop reinstalls I2S driver twice per chime
confirmed.claim: Boot installs I2S at 16000 Hz mono (Audio.cpp:65-70). Audio::playPop() sets 8000 Hz (Audio.cpp:894), so configureI2S()'s cache (Audio.cpp:131-136) MISSES: the driver is uninstalled and reinstalled (~8 KB of internal DMA-capable RAM freed and re-taken, per the measured note at Audio.cpp:113-121), and restore() after the pop flips the rate back to 16000 for a SECOND uninstall/reinstall. So the first text-arrival chime after boot — precisely a first-half-hour event, correlating with the DROP line's sip/app context — churns two ~8 KB free/alloc cycles interleaved with SIP/mirror-poll allocations, a credible source of a one-time ~5 KB largest-block step (the same mechanism the code itself measured as 15,648→8,200 when music changed the rate). Evidence quality: mechanism confirmed in code + prior on-hardware measurement of the same class; the specific attribution to the logged steps is a hypothesis. Low-risk confirmation/fix: resample /pop.pcm to 16 kHz (or set the pop's rate to the boot rate) so the cache hits and the pop allocates nothing; or first just correlate the DROP timestamps with 'NOTIFY: buzz' log_e lines, which are already printed adjacent (WiPhone.ino:1536).

confirmed.title: findMessage shallow-copies IniFile part2 into part1: aliasing, double free
confirmed.claim: Messages::findMessage takes `IniFile& part` (bound to part1 by all three callers: deleteMessage:1141, setRead:1228, ingestMirrored:1056) and does `part = part1; ... part = part2;` intending 'point at the cached partition'. But IniFile/Config/LinearArray define NO copy assignment (grep confirms; LinearArray.h:127-131 owns raw `T* arrayDyn`, Config owns `LinearArray<Section*>` whose Sections are deleted in ~Config, NanoINI.cpp:544-548; IniFile owns `char* filenameDyn`, freed in setFilename, Storage.cpp:1445-1450), so `part = part2` is a compiler-generated SHALLOW memberwise copy: part1's old sections leak, and part1 and part2 now share the same Section* array and the same filenameDyn. The very next preload() that reloads part1 (Storage.cpp:741) calls IniFile::load -> setFilename -> unload -> clear(), deleting the shared Sections and freeing the shared filename, then immediately calls part2.unload() (line 743) which deletes the SAME Section pointers again — double free, heap corruption, reset. Reachable whenever setRead/deleteMessage targets a message whose partition is cached in part2, i.e. whenever a paged scan window spans a partition boundary: PARTITION_SIZE=100 < SIP_THREADS_SCAN=120 (sip_threads.h:61), so any inbox over 100 messages puts MessagesApp::markThreadRead on this path. This is a plausible residual cause of the 'reboots while opening conversations' symptom class that fault 4 only partly explained.
